content.text: why is this running on a non-merged pr: https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/actions/runs/38729274057/job/116402739145?pr=65
I’ll check the run’s trigger and workflow conditions. I’m using the pstack why skill to trace why it ran before the PR merged.

It’s running because the workflow explicitly builds and smoke-tests unmerged PRs. [PR #63](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/63) introduced that behavior.

The workflow has two triggers:

- `pull_request` for relevant file changes, including `exposed/**` and `Cargo.lock`, both changed by PR #65.
- `push` to `main` for publishing releases.

For this PR run, Docker builds a local `exposed:pr` image and runs `--help`. Publishing the image, creating tags, and creating GitHub releases are all gated on `github.event_name == 'push'`. [Workflow](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/69b454085976a2910bc453c4e00756dd3d603d02/.github/workflows/release.yml#L3-L17)

I checked the linked job: release-tag allocation and registry login were both skipped. The **“Build and release exposed” name is misleading here**, but this run won’t publish a release.
okay that should be fine then
Yep, it’s behaving as intended. No changes needed.
